findings.reason: the section's promise is that a second launch never releases a tree its first launch holds, and this predicate still releases it whenever the pointer names the tree before the phase leaves `starting`; the predicate must carry the worktree/pid qualifier dispatch_claims.py:559 uses, and the done-when needs an arm for that shape.
findings.text: §5 says the launch-side view keeps a same-run pointer as a claim "unless its phase is still pre-worker (a waiting phase in `WAITING_REQUEST_PHASES` ... or an unlaunched claim phase in `_UNLAUNCHED_CLAIM_PHASES`)", but the full launch pointer is written with `"worktree": worktree["path"]` (`reckon/crew/routing.py`'s caller, `reckon/crew/dispatch.py:2946`) and `"phase": "starting"` (`reckon/crew/dispatch.py:2991`) before the phase moves to `working`, so a same-run pointer naming the tree is classed pre-worker and disregarded; the repository's own claim predicate already refines this (`reckon/crew/dispatch_claims.py:559`: a phase in `_UNLAUNCHED_CLAIM_PHASES` is unlaunched only when the pointer carries neither a worktree nor a pid), and §5 neither mirrors that qualifier nor gives the done-when an arm for a `starting` pointer that names the tree

findings.reason: a dispatch pass reads declared relationships, not prose, so without one the two sections can be dispatched into the same functions and each would have to be re-reviewed against the other; a declared link (or a `plan-after`/`data-links` entry) is what prevents that.
findings.text: §5 hands duplicate-admission prevention to `a-reexec-never-orphans-a-dispatch` in prose only, and that plan's launch-path comment 96 names §5 in return, yet this plan declares no relationship to it and both sections would edit the same launch functions (`_create_*`/`_remove_*` in `reckon/crew/routing.py`) if dispatched together
